title: Choose Solvin's new visual world
question: Which world should shape a founder-led portfolio that wins trust by showing the work?

options.label: The Proofing Room
options.lineage: photographic contact sheets and professional proofing tables
options.thesis: Projects arrive as evidence on a dark proofing table, then expand into full working stories.
options.viewport: A nearly full-screen project frame sits under a restrained founder statement; scrolling advances through interface, decision, and outcome frames like selecting proofs.
options.risk: It needs excellent project imagery or the proofing metaphor will expose thin material.

raised.raise: Every reveal must explain how the system works, not merely change the picture.
One precise signal color marks progress and active state.
Display typography receives one moment of real scale and confidence.

options.label: The Working Monograph
options.lineage: architectural monographs and independent design journals
options.thesis: Solvin reads like a rigorously edited book of working systems, with each project given room to speak.
options.viewport: A blunt statement and one oversized live project specimen share the opening spread; the portfolio continues as chapters rather than cards.
options.risk: This is the most familiar direction and can become tasteful but forgettable without exceptional pacing.

options.label: The Systems Section
options.thesis: Each project is cut open in section so a business owner can see the people, decisions, data, and software working together.
options.viewport: A continuous cutaway of a business workflow transforms as the visitor scrolls, ending as the finished Solvin product interface.
options.case: It identifies with real business operations and makes Solvin's systems thinking unusually easy to understand.
options.risk: The diagrams must remain human and legible rather than looking like engineering documentation.

options.label: The Build Reel
options.thesis: The portfolio unfolds as a controlled sequence of before, intervention, and working result.
options.viewport: A horizontal project strip scrubs with scroll while short captions explain what changed in each frame.
options.case: It offers the strongest cinematic motion, but the distressed material is less naturally aligned with Solvin's precision.
options.risk: Film texture can read as an effect pasted over software rather than a durable identity.

options.label: The Hard Cut
options.thesis: Projects hit as bold numbered episodes with decisive visual cuts.
options.viewport: An oversized project title collides with a product silhouette and numbered session index.
options.case: Memorable and energetic, but it speaks louder than the founder-led brand should.
options.kept: Motion should use decisive scene changes instead of generic fade-ins.
options.risk: It can overwhelm plain-language business communication.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A polished founder studio with a clear headline, capability list, project cards, testimonials later, and a contact CTA.
canonCard.viewport: A conventional split hero followed by a card-based portfolio.
canonCard.risk: Easy to understand, but difficult to remember or distinguish from another capable software studio.
